topics.name: British study in depth 1A Conflict and Upheaval: England, 1337–1381
points: England in the fourteenth century: society, the Church, the wool trade, position of women, rich and poor
Start of the Hundred Years' War: English lands overseas, Franco-Scottish alliance, Edward III's claim, Philip VI, Aquitaine
Course of the war: chevauchées and the longbow, Crécy, Calais, Poitiers, the Black Prince, Treaty of Brétigny
The Black Death in the short term: arrival, spread, plague strains, contemporary explanations
Legacy of the Black Death: population fall, labour shortage, Statute of Labourers, wages and rents
Causes of peasant discontent: serfdom, John Ball, the French wars, the Poll Tax; Wat Tyler and the events of 1381
Significance of the Peasants' Revolt: broken promises, wage control, decline of serfdom

topics.name: British study in depth 1B The Elizabethan Age, 1558–1603
points: Elizabethan government: Court, Privy Council, local government, Parliament, taxation and free speech
Lifestyles of rich and poor: homes and fashion, causes of poverty, vagrancy, the 1601 Poor Law
Popular entertainment: sports, entertainment of the rich, the Elizabethan theatre and attitudes to it
The problem of religion: the 1559 Settlement, the 'Middle Way', Acts of Supremacy and Uniformity
The Catholic threat: excommunication 1570, recusancy, Northern Earls, Ridolfi, Throckmorton and Babington plots, Mary Queen of Scots
The Spanish Armada: causes, war in the Netherlands, events in the Channel, fireships at Calais, results
The Puritan threat: Puritan challenge to the Settlement, opposition in Parliament, government measures

topics.name: British study in depth 1C Empire, Reform and War: Britain, 1890–1918
points: The Second Boer War: causes, guerrilla war, scorched earth and concentration camps, British attitudes
Political developments: the Liberals, 1909 People's Budget, 1911 Parliament Act, trade unions, rise of Labour
Social reform: Booth and Rowntree, education, Old Age Pensions 1908, National Insurance Act 1911
Women's suffrage: Fawcett and the Suffragists, the Pankhursts and Suffragettes, Emily Davison, the 1918 Act
Culture and fashion: Hardy, Shaw, Wells, Potter, music hall, cinema, sport
The Western Front: tactics, new technology, a case study battle (Ypres, Somme or Verdun), trench life
Impact of the First World War at home: recruitment and conscription, propaganda, women, DORA, attitudes by 1918

topics.name: British study in depth 1D Austerity, Affluence and Discontent: Britain, 1951–1979
points: Britain in the early 1950s: austerity and rationing, housing, nationalised industries, welfare costs
The end of austerity: new towns, rising wages, Macmillan and Wilson, motorways, Beeching, comprehensive schools
Popular entertainment and fashion: music, pop groups, television, American influence, youth fashions
Changing lives of women: labour-saving devices, divorce, abortion, the Pill, equal opportunities, women's liberation
Changing attitudes to authority: the permissive society, abolition of the death penalty, Profumo, CND, 1968 protests
Immigration: Nationality Acts, Windrush, Notting Hill 1958, Enoch Powell, race relations laws
Political and economic problems in the 1970s: Heath and the three-day week, Winter of Discontent, Northern Ireland, the 1979 election

topics.name: Non-British study in depth 1E The Crusades, c.1095–1149
points: The power of the papacy: papal reform, Cluny, pilgrimage, the Investiture Contest
The birth of the Crusades: Seljuk Turks, Urban II, Council of Clermont, indulgences, motives of crusaders
The First Crusade: role of Byzantium, early battles, siege of Antioch, capture of Jerusalem
The Crusader Kingdoms: Edessa, Antioch, Tripoli and Jerusalem; relations with Muslims and Jews
The Second Crusade: reasons, participants and causes of failure
The importance of the Crusades: the crusading orders, castles, interpretations of the Crusades
Social and cultural effects: religious intolerance, trade, science, language, political impact on Europe

topics.name: Non-British study in depth 1F The Voyages of Discovery and Conquest of the Americas, 1492–1522
points: Reasons for the voyages: Spanish and Portuguese ambitions, routes to Asia, trade, religion, technology
The voyages of Columbus: 1492–93, settlement of Hispaniola, treatment of native peoples
The explorers: Diaz, da Gama, Vespucci, Magellan's voyage 1519–22, Spanish settlement of Central America
The Aztec civilisation: rule, tribute, beliefs, codices, sacrifice, Tenochtitlan
Hernán Cortés: relations with Velázquez, expedition to Mexico, indigenous alliances, Cholula massacre
The defeat of the Aztecs: Montezuma, Spanish expulsion, siege of Tenochtitlan, founding of Mexico City
Effects of the conquest: disease, treatment of natives, Christianity, trade, wealth and inflation

topics.name: Non-British study in depth 1G Germany in Transition, 1919–1939
points: Impact of the First World War: Versailles, weaknesses of Weimar, putsches, Ruhr occupation and hyperinflation 1923
Recovery of Weimar: Stresemann, Dawes and Young Plans, Locarno, League of Nations, US loans
The end of the Weimar Republic: impact of the Depression, Hitler's appeal, the SA, propaganda 1929–32
Consolidation of power 1933–34: Reichstag Fire, Enabling Act, Night of the Long Knives, Hitler as Führer
Nazi economic, social and racial policy: unemployment, workers, women, education, Hitler Youth, persecution of Jews
Terror and persuasion: SS and Gestapo, Goebbels, rallies, radio, cinema, censorship
Hitler's foreign policy: rearmament, Rhineland, Anschluss, Sudetenland, Nazi-Soviet Pact

topics.name: Non-British study in depth 1H The USA: A Nation of Contrasts, 1910–1929
points: Immigration: the Open Door, restriction laws, the Red Scare, Palmer Raids, Sacco and Vanzetti
Religion and race: Bible Belt and Monkey Trial, Native Americans, segregation, the KKK, NAACP, UNIA
Crime and corruption: Prohibition, Al Capone, St Valentine's Day Massacre, corruption scandals
The economic boom: impact of WWI, mass production, hire purchase, electrification, laissez-faire
The end of prosperity: overproduction, speculation and the Wall Street Crash
Popular entertainment: cinema, film stars, jazz, radio, speakeasies
The role of women: impact of WWI, flappers, feminism, opposition to change

topics.name: Period study 2A The Development of the USA, 1929–2000
points: Economic downturn and recovery: Wall Street Crash, the Depression, Roosevelt and the New Deal
Impact of the Second World War and post-war change: affluence, consumerism, suburbs, 'poverty amidst plenty'
Civil Rights 1941–1970: desegregation of schools, Montgomery, King and Malcolm X, civil rights laws
Political change 1960–2000: Kennedy, Nixon and Watergate, Reagan, Bush and Clinton
Social change 1950–2000: music, media, youth culture and protest, the role of women
Cold War rivalry 1945–73: Truman Doctrine, containment, Berlin, Cuban Missile Crisis, Vietnam
The search for world peace since 1970: détente, arms limitation, end of the Cold War, Iran, Gulf War

topics.name: Period study 2B The Development of Germany, 1919–1991
points: Weimar Germany: the war and Versailles, opposition, Stresemann, foreign relations
The rise of the Nazis to 1934: Nazi support, Hitler as Chancellor, steps to dictatorship, the police state
Life under the Nazis 1933–39: the economy, workers, women, children and education, the Jews
Life during the Second World War: the Home Front, opposition, treatment of Jews, impact of defeat
West and East Germany 1949–1991: division, Western recovery, repression in the East
Cold War relations: Berlin Blockade and Airlift, the Berlin Wall, alliances, Brandt and Ostpolitik
Reconciliation and reunification: collapse in Eastern Europe, Kohl, fall of the Wall, reunification 1990

topics.name: Period study 2C The Development of the USSR, 1924–1991
points: The rule of Stalin 1924–53: the leadership contest, cult of Stalin, propaganda, censorship and terror
Life under Stalin: collectivisation, de-kulakisation, Five Year Plans, the changing role of women
Impact of the Second World War: Barbarossa, Leningrad and Stalingrad, reconstruction
Cold War relations 1945–91: NATO and the Warsaw Pact, arms race, Berlin, Cuba, Afghanistan
Political developments 1953–85: Khrushchev and de-Stalinisation, Brezhnev, changes of leader
Gorbachev's reforms: perestroika, glasnost, democratisation, relations with the West
The collapse of communism: unrest in Eastern Europe, nationalism, Yeltsin, end of the USSR

topics.name: Period study 2D The Development of the UK, 1919–1990
points: Britain in the Twenties: post-war adjustment, welfare, Ireland, the General Strike, the status of women
Life during the Depression: unemployment in staple industries, the dole and Means Test, hunger marches, new industries
The Home Front: preparations, the Blitz, evacuation, rationing, women, propaganda
Post-war Britain 1945–60: the NHS, nationalisation, education, growing affluence
The 'Swinging Sixties': popular culture, consumerism, permissiveness, immigration and race
The 'Stuttering Seventies': Northern Ireland, Europe, Scottish and Welsh nationalism, Winter of Discontent
The Thatcher years 1979–90: recession and recovery, Falklands, Miners' Strike, privatisation

topics.name: Thematic study 2E Changes in Crime and Punishment in Britain, c.500 to the present day
points: Causes of crime: poverty and war, religious change, industrialisation, modern violence and anti-social behaviour
The nature of crimes: medieval crimes, vagrancy, heresy and treason, smuggling, industrial crime, motor, computer and terrorist crime
Enforcing law and order: Saxon communal duty, manorial and royal courts, parish duties, the police
Combating crime: JPs, Bow Street Runners, Peel and the Metropolitan Police 1829, community policing
Methods of punishment: medieval punishments, transportation, prison reform, silent and separate systems, probation and parole
Attitudes to crime and punishment: retribution, deterrence, reform, abolition of the death penalty, rehabilitation
Historic environment: the specified site (2026–27 Policing in Liverpool c.1787–1900; 2028–29 Criminal gangs in Birmingham c.1870–1945)

topics.name: Thematic study 2F Changes in Health and Medicine in Britain, c.500 to the present day
points: Causes of illness and disease: poverty, hygiene and plague, cholera and typhoid, 20th-century infections
Attempts to prevent illness: medieval methods, inoculation, Jenner and vaccination, bacteriology
Attempts to treat and cure: herbal remedies, barber-surgeons, Simpson and anaesthetics, Lister and antiseptics, antibiotics, transplants
Advances in medical knowledge: humours and astrology, Vesalius, Paré, Harvey, germ theory, scanning, DNA
Developments in patient care: monasteries, hospitals, Nightingale, Liberal reforms, Beveridge and the NHS
Public health and welfare: medieval hygiene, industrial towns, Chadwick, housing and pollution, modern health campaigns
Historic environment: the specified site (2026–27 Letchworth Garden City c.1903–present; 2028–29 Norwich and the plague 1349–1667)

topics.name: Thematic study 2G The Development of Warfare in Britain, c.500 to the present day
points: Causes of war: religion (Crusades), politics (English Civil War), nationalism (WWII), ideology (Cold War)
Changes in tactics and strategy: Saxon and Viking warfare, medieval tactics, linear tactics, trench warfare, guerrilla warfare
Training and recruitment: feudal service, Tudor armies, New Model Army, press gangs, conscription, National Service
Changes in technology: siege warfare, longbows and firearms, industrial weapons, tanks and aircraft, nuclear and hi-tech weapons
The development of naval warfare: Tudor navy and the Armada, the Royal Navy, Napoleonic and World Wars
The role of women in war: medieval and early modern women, nursing, the Home Fronts, frontline roles
Historic environment: the specified site (2026–27 Royal Dockyards, Chatham c.1567–1984; 2028–29 Aldershot Garrison 1854–present)

topics.name: Thematic study 2H Changes in Entertainment and Leisure in Britain, c.500 to the present day
points: The development of sport: medieval sports, jousting and hunting, spectator sport, professionalism, sponsorship and media
Holidays and travel: feast days, the Grand Tour, railways and seaside resorts, Bank Holiday Act 1871, holiday camps, package holidays
Popular entertainment on stage and screen: mystery plays, Elizabethan theatre, music halls, cinema, television
Popular entertainment in sound and music: medieval music, brass bands, radio, jazz, rock and roll, 1960s pop
Children's entertainment: games and toys, comics, radio and TV, computer games
Cruelty in sport and entertainment: hunting, public executions, bull-baiting, bare-knuckle fighting, animal welfare
Historic environment: the specified site (2026–27 Glastonbury Festival c.1970–present; 2028–29 Scarborough)
